titre: The tragic breakdown of multilateralism (Le Monde)
description: Compréhension de l'éditorial, synonymes, expressions soulignées et vocabulaire.

questions.question: According to the editorial, what does the escalation between Israel and Hezbollah highlight?
choix: the end of the General Assembly
the success of UN peacekeeping in Lebanon
the strength of the Security Council
the impotence of the United Nations
questions.explication: « highlights the impotence of the United Nations ».

questions.question: Which two major conflicts have highlighted the paralysis of the Security Council? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: the destruction of Gaza after the massacres of October 7

questions.question: By whose vetoes has the Security Council been blocked? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.explication: « blocked by Russian and American vetoes ».

questions.question: What did the General Assembly vote for on September 18 (2024)?
choix: an end « within 12 months » to the Israeli occupation of the Palestinian territories
the enlargement of the Security Council
questions.explication: Une décision symbolique que l'Assemblée est incapable de faire appliquer.

questions.question: Why does the UN look « like a shadow theater »?
choix: because the General Assembly's symbolic decisions are never translated into reality
because its meetings take place at night
questions.explication: a shadow theater = un théâtre d'ombres : une apparence d'action sans effet réel.

questions.question: For which countries did Russia use its veto in 2023? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.explication: « to the benefit of its customers ».

questions.question: What did Moscow block in March (2024)?
choix: the renewal of the UN sanctions monitoring mandate against North Korea (Pyongyang)
questions.explication: La Corée du Nord était devenue l'un de ses fournisseurs d'armes.

questions.question: Why did Russia protect the Pyongyang regime?
choix: it is a founding member of the UN
it had become one of Russia's arms suppliers
questions.explication: « which had become one of its arms suppliers ».

questions.question: Which UN bodies still play an indispensable role, according to experts?
choix: UN agencies dealing with world hunger or the plight of refugees
questions.explication: Les agences (PAM, HCR…) aident « those left behind ».

questions.question: How has the Security Council changed since its creation?
choix: only a slight modification: four non-permanent seats were added
Germany and Japan became permanent members
questions.explication: Passage de 11 à 15 membres (1965) : composition devenue « une caricature de l'état du monde ».

questions.question: What did the United States propose on September 12 (2024)? (plusieurs réponses)
choix: a seat for the small island states on the front line of global warming
a rotating seat for Latin America
giving the new African seats a veto
questions.explication: Mais « with no question of these seats being vetoed » → « shaky position ».

questions.question: Which « imploding nations » are mentioned? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.explication: « from Sudan to Haiti via Myanmar ».

questions.question: Which crises call for multilateral responses, according to the text? (plusieurs réponses)
questions.explication: Le paradoxe : l'ONU est abandonnée alors que les crises se multiplient.

questions.question: What is « the paradox » mentioned at the end?
choix: the UN has more members but fewer resolutions
the UN is being abandoned just when crises that need multilateral responses are multiplying
the UN is richer but less useful

questions.question: What is the political echelon of the UN, according to the text?
questions.explication: « its political echelon, the Security Council ».

questions.question: Which newspaper published this editorial?
a shadow theater
questions.verso: un théâtre d'ombres — an illusion: actions that look important but have no real effect. Dans le texte : « make the UN look even more like a shadow theater »

questions.question: Explain « a shadow theater ».
choix: a collective reaction coordinated between several countries
to be in an uncertain situation where nothing is decided
to become empty, exhausted; to lose its substance
an illusion: actions that look important but have no real effect
questions.explication: a shadow theater = un théâtre d'ombres.

questions.question: It's high time to revive the mechanisms that have ___ up. (se gripper)
Heads of state and government are due to take to the ___ in the last week of September.
…in a ritual that has long since run ___.
The deadly escalation between Israel and Hezbollah once again ___ the impotence of the United Nations.
…the destruction of Gaza in ___ for the unprecedented massacres of Israeli civilians by Hamas.
This ___ multilateralism has no alternatives. (enlisé)
Russia's ___ use of its veto to the benefit of its customers shows this. (vaste)
UN agencies dealing with world hunger or the ___ of refugees continue to play an indispensable role.
The much-needed reform of the Security Council is, alas, in ___.
This shaky position explains the ___ of response to this proposal.
…which would change absolutely nothing in the current ___. (impasse)
The abandonment of the UN coincides with a growing number of crises: ___ nations, from Sudan to Haiti.
All call for ___ responses.
What is multilateralism in the context of the UN?
questions.verso: Multilateralism means that many countries work together through common institutions to solve shared problems. At the UN it relies on inclusivity (all 193 states have a voice), equality (one state, one vote in the General Assembly) and cooperation (collective responses to wars, pandemics, climate change).

questions.question: Do you share the writer's pessimism? (arguments)
questions.verso: YES: Security Council paralysed by vetoes (Ukraine, Gaza), symbolic GA resolutions, reform in limbo, Russia protecting allies. BUT: UN agencies (WFP, UNHCR) remain indispensable, the GA still expresses world opinion, crises (pandemics, climate, migration) make multilateralism more necessary than ever, UN80 reform.
